tools.name: list_pages
tools.description: List the pages in the project this MCP key is bound to, each with its id, `path`, `language`, full field SCHEMA, pageType (singleton|dynamic), and status. Use it to verify WHERE content lands and to read field keys/types before set_page_content / add_field.

tools.name: get_page
tools.description: Get one page INCLUDING its full field schema (keys, types, nested group/repeater children), pageType, `path` and `language`. A field with `stale: true` is one the build no longer renders: kept, hidden in the editor. `entryDraft.draftPending`: its field values have unpublished edits (`keys`). Read this before set_page_content so you write correctly-keyed values, or before add_field so you know the existing keys.

pageId.description: page id or path ('/de/about'); a bare slug only when one page has it

branchId.description: content branch id (from list_branches); omit to work on main

tools.name: create_page
tools.description: Create a page with its own typed schema. Supports pageType 'singleton' (exactly one entry — Home, About, Contact) and 'dynamic' (many entries sharing the schema — Blog posts, Products). Project-scoped from the key. Additive — does not delete or overwrite existing pages. FIRST read the page's real markup and DECOMPOSE it into a destructured tree: each visual section becomes a nested field — a fixed grouped block → type 'group', a repeating list of items (cards, testimonials, features, FAQs) → type 'repeater' — each carrying its own child `fields`. Do NOT flatten sections into many flat top-level fields. Build the full nested tree, then call this once. Field keys are unique among siblings: 'title' may repeat in two sections, not twice in one. Prose fields (headings, body copy, descriptions) are created as RICH TEXT by default; pass richText:false for values that must stay bare strings — hrefs, slugs, ids, emails. That tree is the page's SCHEMA — what it holds. STRUCTURE (separate from schema): a page is composed of SECTIONS. NEVER build a page out of loose top-level heading/text/image/button/spacer blocks — they cannot be moved, duplicated or swapped as a unit, the visual editor cannot outline or name them, and every one of them becomes its own section in the editor. A hero of a headline, a lede and two CTAs is ONE section, not four. TWO SHAPES, and the choice is about REUSE. (1) A band that appears on more than one page, or that needs layout variants, is a COMPONENT with a `sectionType` — see create_component. Components sharing a `sectionType` are that section's VARIANTS (one Hero: 'Centered' for the home page and 'Two-column' for about, same prop keys so a swap keeps the content). This is also the only shape the editor's 'Add a section' picker can insert, and the only one that gets a family name and a variant switcher. (2) A genuinely one-off band on a single page is a `section` BLOCK whose `props.children` hold its blocks. THE TRADEOFF, stated in the present tense because it is real today: inside a component, ONLY the leaves a declared prop TARGETS are click-to-edit on the canvas — each declared prop's `target` is re-keyed to that PLACEMENT's own override address, so editing it changes this page and not the shared definition. A prop with no `target` still SHOWS as a dock control, but its override reaches no rendered slot, so editing it changes nothing on the page. Copy that no prop points at is worse still: no binding and no control, unreachable from click-to-edit AND from the dock, changeable only by editing the component definition, which rewrites every page that places it. A `section` block's children stay click-to-edit unconditionally. So when you choose a component, DECLARE A PROP — WITH A `target` — for every string, link and image a marketer will ever touch; a component with un-propped editable copy is the defect, not the component. In the dock an unset prop shows EMPTY and inherits the definition's default, so set props explicitly when you want the current copy visible there. An IMPORTED site's components are its own (read the repo); its nav, footer and modals are the Layout. On a blank site, do not hand-write a band's JSON: start from a built-in section blueprint (list_components returns locked `builtin:*` blueprints with no projectId — hero-centered, hero-split, feature-grid-three, cta-banner and more), each already rooted in a `section` block with its editable leaves declared as props. INLINE its blockJson as a `section` block for a one-off band; for a recurring band, materialize it with create_component `from` so it becomes project-scoped before implementation validation, Output or publication. Direct `builtin:*` component references exist only for legacy delivery compatibility. Two consecutive call-to-action buttons are two sibling `button` blocks inside the same section — never a `columns` block, which is a `repeat(N,1fr)` grid and would stretch each CTA to half the container. Buttons are inline-level and flow side by side on their own.

title.description: display title of the page, e.g. 'Home'

slug.description: URL-safe path segment, unique per project, e.g. 'home'

pageType.description: 'singleton' = exactly one entry (Home, About, Contact); 'dynamic' = many entries sharing this schema (Blog posts, Products). Defaults to singleton.

blockJson.description: the page's VISUAL composition — how a components-first page is built. Place one `component` block per section: {type:'component', id:'<stable>', props:{componentId:'<id from create_component>'}}. The component must be PUBLISHED (publish_component) or it renders as nothing on the live site. Independent of `fields`, which is a typed schema for a site's own code to read.

type.description: block type; section/slider/tabs/columns nest child blocks

props.description: per-type props by block type: §5 of bettercms://playbook/schema (text/richtext {html}, NOT {text}; button {text, href, variant?, size? sm|md|lg, fullWidth?}; component {componentId, overrides?}). Containers nest blocks to any depth.

style.description: design tokens: theme, bg (none|surface|muted|accent|dark|custom), bgCustom hex, paddingTop/paddingBottom/paddingSides px, contentWidth (narrow|default|wide|full), align, corner, shadow, borderTop/borderBottom, border (all four sides, in the text colour), hideOn [mobile|tablet|desktop] (all three hides it on the page: kept in the draft, never published). A real marketing band is a `section` block carrying bg + padding + contentWidth.

window.description: {from?, until?}, ISO 8601 with offset: shown only between the two instants; null clears (skill publishing).

data.description: a SINGLETON's field VALUES keyed by field key — seeds its entry in the same call. If any value is refused the page is still created, none of `data` is saved, and the result names ENTRY_SEED_FAILED with the per-field reasons: fix them and write with set_page_content.

locale.description: language, a BCP-47 tag (zh-CN → zh-cn), one of the project's locales; null = the default

translationOf.description: the SOURCE id this translates (never a translation); null unlinks. One per locale: the translation sets locale and translationOf

folderId.description: the URL folder the page lives in, a page's `folderId` from list_pages; omitted = the site root. A translation goes in its language's folder (the folderId of the site's other /de/ pages)

branchId.description: content branch id (from list_branches); omit to work on main

key.description: machine field key, unique among its SIBLINGS (the top level, or one group's children): two siblings with one key are refused, the same key in two groups ('hero.title', 'faq.title') is fine. Keys derived from an imported site may contain hyphens ('hero-h1-welcome'): address them exactly as returned.

label.description: human label shown in the editor

type.description: field type. 'button' is ONE call to action, value {label, href, variant? (a Button family look), size?, arrow?, icon?, newTab?, rel?, fullWidth?} (arrow:false, icon:null off): never a text field beside a link field. A link or button href: a URL string or {type: url|page|entry|email|phone|anchor|file, href, title?, newTab?, rel?, section?, ref: page/entry id}.

required.description: an entry cannot be saved without a value — set it only where the site genuinely cannot render without one

richText.description: prose formatting. DEFAULTS TO TRUE for 'text': the field is created as rich text so editors can bold, link and format it on the canvas, and the API returns rich text (render with rich() from @bettercms-ai/sdk; plain() for titles and meta). Pass false for a value that is NOT prose and must stay a bare string — a URL/href, a slug, an id, an email, a phone number, a CSS class, an icon name. A link stored as rich text will not work as an href.

options.description: choices when type is 'select'. A plain string, or {label, value, icon?, description?} when the stored value differs from what the editor shows (e.g. {label:'Sold out', value:'soldOut'}); icon a dock name, description one line ≤140.

config.description: per-type config: reference {contentModelId}, multi-reference {contentModelId,min,max}, repeater {minItems, maxItems} (the list's item limits; the editor shows 'max N' and stops Add there), array {itemType: text|number|date|image|link|richtext}, date {includeTime, timezone}, modular|slot {blockSlugs: ['quote','gallery'], minItems?, maxItems?} (slot: playbook §5) — blockSlugs is REQUIRED, non-empty, and each slug must name an existing kind:'block' model; richtext {inline:true, hostTag:'h2', accept:['h2','p','b','i','u','link'], features:['bold','italic','underline','link','headings'], allowMultipleParagraphs:false} — for a field bound to ONE element on the page: `hostTag` is that element's tag and `accept` must name it, so the editor's block-style control opens already showing 'Heading 2' instead of 'Paragraph'. Name exactly ONE heading level: publish refuses an <h3> value bound to an <h2> rather than nesting one heading inside the other. Keep 'p' in `accept` or the sanitiser strips a block demoted to Paragraph; richtext article blocks and references {posts?, authors?}: playbook/schema §5c; limits: text/longtext {minLength,maxLength,pattern,patternMessage}, richtext {minLength,maxLength}, number {validation:{min,max}}, array {minItems,maxItems}, tags {min,max}, rating {min,max,step}. Undocumented keys open the classic editor.

fields.description: NESTED child fields — REQUIRED for type 'group' (one nested object, a Non-Repeatable Zone like blog_hero → heading, description, hero_image) and type 'repeater' (a repeatable array of such objects, a Repeatable Zone / section-list like testimonials → quote, author). A section with repeating items is a 'repeater'; a fixed grouped block is a 'group'. Recurse to any depth — do NOT flatten zones into separate top-level fields.

helpText.description: shown under the field: one line (aim ~60 chars, max 80) on what belongs there, from the section's source and purpose; never its label, its value or a generic role sentence. null when the label says it all. Omitted: none (the platform writes no help)

showIf.description: conditional visibility — hide this field until another field has a given value (e.g. show `external_url` only when `link_type` is 'external'). Admin-only: it changes what an author SEES, never what is stored or delivered. Rules reference fields by BARE KEY, and the key namespace is flat, so the key must exist on this model.

collapsed.description: start this panel collapsed. Use it for long optional sections.

preview.description: how ONE ITEM summarises itself when collapsed. Every slot names a CHILD KEY of THIS field/prop (a dotted path reads into it: 'author.name'). title.description: CHILD KEY whose value titles a collapsed row

subtitle.description: CHILD KEY whose value is the row's second line (e.g. 'level' → 'Heading · h2')

media.description: CHILD KEY whose value is the row's thumbnail (image/file/url all work)

fallback.description: a literal row label while the title child is empty ('Untitled question'), not a key

icon.description: the row's icon while it has no media, a dock icon name

layout.description: how the ITEMS are arranged. Omit (≡ 'list') for rows of text; 'grid' for items whose thumbnail is the thing you scan — a gallery, a logo wall, a team; 'table' for up to 3 scalar columns. Same placement rule as `preview`. reorderable.description: omit (≡ true) unless the order is PART OF THE MEANING. `false` LOCKS the list — a 'three steps' band that must stay three steps in that order, a nav whose order is semantic, a timeline. Valid only where there is a list to lock.

control.description: editor control for a LEAF. Omit for the default. 'segmented' on a select with a few short options (alignment, theme, size); 'slider' on a number that has config.min < config.max (opacity, columns); 'rating' on a number with config.min, max and step; 'dropdown'/'radio'/'grid'/'cards' on a select ('cards' also a multiselect); 'switch'/'checkbox' on a boolean ('checkbox' also a multiselect). Anything else is refused with the rule named.

icon.description: the branch row's icon, a name from bettercms://icons/dock. Nesting fields only.

itemLabel.description: what ONE item is called ('Slide'): the add button, crumbs and empty state. Nesting fields and lists. V2 itemNoun goes here.

itemName.description: a list's item type name (an identifier). Lists only.

itemTitle.description: a list's item type title. Lists only.

rows.description: the lines a text box opens with. text / longtext only.

placeholder.description: ghost text, a field of any type. A prop uses its own `placeholder`.

synced.description: the value comes from this global; edits apply everywhere.

valueShape.description: a link / image / button writes a plain string or the object.

reference.description: a json field holding a live vendor item: the integration's slug and reference key.

access.description: who sees (view: developer-only) and who changes (edit) it, gated in the editor. The enforced lock is readOnly:'developer'.

hidden.description: true: never shown in the form (a system value). A conditional hide is showIf.

blocks.description: modular only: per block slug, {icon?, preview?, openMode?} for its rows.

input.description: a custom dock input by NAME (the project's bettercms/inputs/<name>.tsx), a last resort after `control`, `preview` and groups. `writes`: sibling field keys it may also write, nothing else. Setting or changing it needs `confirmed: true`, sent only after the user approved it.

fieldsetId.description: id of one of this model's `fieldsets` (create_content_model / update_content_model). The field is shown inside that card in the editor. Editor-only: never changes what is stored or delivered.

placement.description: where the control sits in the entry editor: 'title' the entry's heading, 'cover' its lead image, 'excerpt' the summary, 'body' the document body, 'inline' or 'panel'. Omit to let the editor decide. Editor-only.

defaultValue.description: the value a new entry starts with

searchable.description: omit (≡ true) to index this field for site search; false excludes it

unique.description: true: no two entries of this model may hold the same value (compared trimmed and case-insensitively). On a repeater child such as a variant SKU it also covers every row of every entry. Only on text, longtext, slug, email, phone, link, number, select, reference and date; on a list it means no item repeats. A clash is refused with 409 `unique_conflict`.

readOnly.description: 'developer' = the value and this lock change only with schema access (needs lockReason); true = an editor marker

lockReason.description: which system owns the value (≤ 200 chars)

helpMore.description: longer help behind the ⓘ next to the label, when one helpText line cannot carry it

advanced.description: true = a rare or developer setting: it collects in a closed 'Advanced' section

recommendedMax.description: a SOFT limit (characters, items or value): the editor warns past it, never refuses

openMode.description: object/array/group/repeater: how the value (or each row) opens: 'inline', 'drill', 'popover' or 'dialog'

ai.description: true = the editor offers its AI assist on this field

tools.name: create_content_model
tools.description: Create a content model — a reusable schema for a dynamic collection (Blog, Products, Testimonials). A collection is only for items one template route repeats (/blog/:slug: set urlPattern). A single page's copy (home, about, contact, pricing, legal) is page fields in sections (add_field with pageId / set_page_content), never a one-entry collection. `fields` may NEST: type 'group' = one nested object of child fields; type 'repeater' = a repeatable array of child objects. Put child fields in each group/repeater's own `fields` (any depth). Pass kind:'block' to create a BLOCK type instead — see that argument. `fieldsets` ([{id, name}]) are the model's editor cards; a field joins one with `fieldsetId`. The slug must be unique in this project and branch: a taken one is refused with 409 `slug_taken` and free `suggestions`. 🔴 A field of type 'text' is created as RICH TEXT unless you send `richText: false` on it. Send `richText: false` for every value that is not prose: a name used as a title, a URL, slug, id, SKU, email, phone, CSS class or icon name.

description.description: for editors: what it is and holds; omitted: written for you

urlPattern.description: the public URL of one entry, e.g. '/blog/:slug'. Must start with '/' and contain ':slug' exactly once ('{slug}' is refused). Drives RSS item links and the automatic 301 when an entry's slug changes. null clears it.

kind.description: 'model' (default) = a collection with its own entries. 'block' = a type that exists only to be stacked inside another model's 'modular' field — it holds no entries, and create_content_entry against it is refused. Create blocks FIRST, then the model whose modular field lists their slugs. Cannot be changed later.

fields.description: the model's typed schema fields. 'group'/'repeater' NEST their child fields (any depth) — don't flatten zones into top-level fields.

A field joins one with `fieldsetId`. Editor-only: never changes what is stored or delivered.

tools.name: create_content_entry
tools.description: Create a content entry under a model. A collection is only for items one template route repeats (/blog/:slug: set urlPattern). A single page's copy (home, about, contact, pricing, legal) is page fields in sections (add_field with pageId / set_page_content), never a one-entry collection. Pass its field VALUES in `data`, keyed by field key — INCLUDE ALL REQUIRED FIELDS (create validates them). New entries are drafts; pass status:'published' to take it live. Read get_content_model first for the field keys and which are required. One entry per call: for volume, run code against the Management API.

contentModelId.description: id of the model this entry belongs to

data.description: field values keyed by field key

locale.description: language, a BCP-47 tag (zh-CN → zh-cn), one of the project's locales; null = the default

translationOf.description: the SOURCE id this translates (never a translation); null unlinks. One per locale: the translation sets locale and translationOf

dryRun.description: validates and reports what would be written; writes nothing

externalKey.description: id in the source system; sent again, it updates that entry's draft or leaves it unchanged

source.description: source URL, kept with the entry

runId.description: your run's id, kept with the entry

branchId.description: content branch id (from list_branches); omit to work on main

tools.name: set_page_content
tools.description: Set a page's field VALUES — the actual content. For a SINGLETON page (Home, About, Site Settings) this creates or updates its one entry, so call it again to edit. `data` is keyed by field key: a nested 'array' (zone) value is an OBJECT { nonRepeatable: { childKey: value }, repeatable: [ { childKey: value } ] }; a primitive 'array' is a plain list; an 'image' value is an asset URL or { url, altText?, focal?, crop? } — focal {x,y} and crop {top,right,bottom,left} (0–1, cut from each edge) frame THIS placement only. Read the schema first with get_page. This is how you populate Home/About/Settings — create_content_entry is for dynamic collections only. Merges by top-level key (a zone value replaces that whole zone); pass replace:true to remove omitted fields. A moved (componentized) field writes to its block; an unowned one is refused (409).

pageId.description: page id or path ('/de/about'); a bare slug only when one page has it

data.description: field values keyed by field key. A nested 'array' (zone) value is an OBJECT { nonRepeatable: { childKey: value, … }, repeatable: [ { childKey: value }, … ] } — nonRepeatable holds the fixed-block values, repeatable is the list of item objects (omit a zone you didn't define). A primitive 'array' (itemType) is a plain list. An 'image' value is an asset URL or asset id (from upload_asset) — the server resolves it to { id, url, name, altText }. Read get_page first to see each field's zones.

replace.description: true replaces the whole entry data, removing omitted fields; default false merges by top-level key

branchId.description: content branch id (from list_branches); omit to work on main

tools.name: list_content_entries
tools.description: List content entries — including drafts — filtered by model and/or page, by field values (`where`), sorted and paged. Use it to SEE existing content before editing. For a singleton page, pass its pageId to get its single entry. A project-scoped connection sees its own project's entries plus workspace-level ones, which it can read but not change. Returns `limit` entries per `page` (50 by default); the summary says which page of how many. Each entry is a SUMMARY (id, slug, title, status, model, page, dates, optimisticVersion, pendingChanges) — read values with get_content_entry, or pass `detail: true` for full rows.

pageId.description: filter by page id (a singleton page has one entry)

externalKey.description: exact externalKey an entry was created with

where.description: field filters: {field: value} is equality, {field: {op: value}} with op eq|ne|gt|gte|lt|lte|contains|in, and an array means `in`. System fields slug, status, publishedAt, locale work anywhere; a data field needs modelId. Compares the served copy (live for published, working for draft)

sort.description: comma list, a leading - sorts descending, e.g. '-publishedAt,title'

page.description: 1-based page of `limit` rows; the response's meta says totalPages

limit.description: entries per page, 1-200; 50 when omitted. Read `meta.totalPages` and ask for the next `page`.

detail.description: true = full rows with every field value and the published copy. Large: read one entry with get_content_entry instead.

branchId.description: content branch id (from list_branches); omit to work on main

tools.name: create_component
tools.description: Create a reusable component from a blockJson tree. THIS IS ALSO HOW A PAGE GETS ITS SECTIONS: set `sectionType` (e.g. 'Hero') and the component becomes a placeable section, selectable in the editor's 'Add a section' picker. Components sharing a `sectionType` are its layout VARIANTS — one Hero with a 'Centered' and a 'Two-column' variant, same prop keys, so a swap keeps the content. CONFIRM the structure with the user first. blockJson is an array of blocks — the same set create_page accepts (heading, text/richtext, image, button, spacer, video, columns, section, slider, tabs, navbar, footer, form, component, collection), NOT a narrower one; `section` nests child blocks in props.children and `columns` in props.columns. `props` declares overridable fields. Returns the new id — render with `<BcmsBlocks>`. Always lands as a DRAFT — call publish_component to put it on the live site; until then it renders as NOTHING there, with no error.  Buttons auto-join the project's Button family; section buttons link to its looks.STRUCTURE (separate from schema): a page is composed of SECTIONS. NEVER build a page out of loose top-level heading/text/image/button/spacer blocks — they cannot be moved, duplicated or swapped as a unit, the visual editor cannot outline or name them, and every one of them becomes its own section in the editor. A hero of a headline, a lede and two CTAs is ONE section, not four. TWO SHAPES, and the choice is about REUSE. (1) A band that appears on more than one page, or that needs layout variants, is a COMPONENT with a `sectionType` — see create_component. Components sharing a `sectionType` are that section's VARIANTS (one Hero: 'Centered' for the home page and 'Two-column' for about, same prop keys so a swap keeps the content). This is also the only shape the editor's 'Add a section' picker can insert, and the only one that gets a family name and a variant switcher. (2) A genuinely one-off band on a single page is a `section` BLOCK whose `props.children` hold its blocks. THE TRADEOFF, stated in the present tense because it is real today: inside a component, ONLY the leaves a declared prop TARGETS are click-to-edit on the canvas — each declared prop's `target` is re-keyed to that PLACEMENT's own override address, so editing it changes this page and not the shared definition. A prop with no `target` still SHOWS as a dock control, but its override reaches no rendered slot, so editing it changes nothing on the page. Copy that no prop points at is worse still: no binding and no control, unreachable from click-to-edit AND from the dock, changeable only by editing the component definition, which rewrites every page that places it. A `section` block's children stay click-to-edit unconditionally. So when you choose a component, DECLARE A PROP — WITH A `target` — for every string, link and image a marketer will ever touch; a component with un-propped editable copy is the defect, not the component. In the dock an unset prop shows EMPTY and inherits the definition's default, so set props explicitly when you want the current copy visible there. An IMPORTED site's components are its own (read the repo); its nav, footer and modals are the Layout. On a blank site, do not hand-write a band's JSON: start from a built-in section blueprint (list_components returns locked `builtin:*` blueprints with no projectId — hero-centered, hero-split, feature-grid-three, cta-banner and more), each already rooted in a `section` block with its editable leaves declared as props. INLINE its blockJson as a `section` block for a one-off band; for a recurring band, materialize it with create_component `from` so it becomes project-scoped before implementation validation, Output or publication. Direct `builtin:*` component references exist only for legacy delivery compatibility. Two consecutive call-to-action buttons are two sibling `button` blocks inside the same section — never a `columns` block, which is a `repeat(N,1fr)` grid and would stretch each CTA to half the container. Buttons are inline-level and flow side by side on their own. A `warnings` entry UNPROPPED_COPY names copy no prop targets, which nobody can edit: add a prop with a `target` for each leaf it lists.

Set this with a library category to make the component selectable in the page editor's 'Add a section' picker. Components sharing one are layout variants of one section.

tools.description: Give up to 50 pages their block composition in ONE call — the same write as update_page's `blockJson`, once per item, and it REPLACES each page's whole block array. Address a page by `pageId` or by `slug`. Each item reports `{ ok, pageId, slug, error }` and a failure does not stop the run. BEFORE writing anything it reads this project's component catalogue once and REFUSES any item placing a componentId the project does not have — its missing sections would render as empty strings with no error anywhere. Writes DRAFTS: publish each page with update_page status:'published' afterwards. A page is composed of SECTIONS: a recurring band is a component with a `sectionType`, a one-off band is a `section` block whose `props.children` hold its blocks — never loose top-level heading/text/image blocks, which no editor can move, name or swap as a unit. tools.name: set_component_source
tools.description: Call this RIGHT AFTER you write or locate a component's code in the app's repository: it records which file renders it, so the dashboard's Output button can preview and validate it with no setup (without it nothing is validated). Record ONLY a file that renders exactly this component from its own fields: a component whose props are this component's field keys (`kind: 'file'`, the default), or a section the codemod extracted with `npx @bettercms-ai/convert --componentize` — a file starting `// @bettercms-ai/convert section` whose props are `{ blockId, bind, overrides, page }` (`kind: 'section'`). Never record a different component that merely contains this markup (e.g. a card that needs a `post` object): it cannot render from these fields and validation fails. If the markup is inline in a page, extract it into a section first. `path` is relative to the app root (e.g. 'src/components/sections/Hero.astro'); `export` is the export name, omitted for a default export. Call it again if the file moves; call clear_component_source if a recorded file is wrong.

Call it after authoring a component and after every validation run. outputReady means the Output renders; publishReady also needs the owner's Visual Approval in the dashboard, which no tool can give.

tools.name: publish_component
tools.description: Publish one project-scoped component variant after its exact implementation evidence and human approval are ready: copy its DRAFT definition to the live copy and re-bake every published page that embeds it. This is the ONLY way a component reaches the live site. Built-in `builtin:*` rows are locked blueprints, not implementations; materialize one with create_component first. Workspace-global component publication is currently fail-closed. Drafts (create_component, update_component) render as NOTHING live, with no error: publish every component you place on a page. 403 PUBLISH_NOT_GRANTED means this connection may author but not publish: say so and let the user publish from the dashboard. 🔴 A 409 COMPONENT_IMPLEMENTATION_NOT_READY is NOT retried and must not be: no tool on this connection can clear it. It asks for exact validation evidence and a human's approval, never of a component you just made with create_component (which ones: skill components). Its `readiness` names what is missing — relay it to the user instead of retrying or routing around it. 422 means publishing would break a Layout that uses it — the response names which.

Apply every fix, rerun, resubmit: only `complete: true` ends a conversion — never report a site converted on less. Apply what you can; the site stays text-match for the rest and flips to declared only when nothing is left for the annotator (never set `declaredBindings` by hand). It is a RECORD, not a release: nothing on the site changes; the meter reads it on the get_binding_report after the next deploy. 🔴 The same run owes two more things (playbook §13 steps 2b and 3b): the `--forms` receipt (a SECOND call, same `briefDigest`) and the `styleEdits` of `convert --verify-styles` inside this receipt; any changed class or style is refused with 409 `style-edits`. tools.name: update_page
tools.description: Edit a page: title, slug, SEO metaTitle/metaDescription, structured data (`schemaType`, `schema`), publish status (draft|published), and `blockJson` (its block composition — passing an array REPLACES the whole array, so read get_page first and send its `optimisticVersion` as `ifMatch`; an object adds or styles ONE section). An answer that starts with `held` is a draft the live page will NOT show until each of `holds` has its `action` taken, and a publish answers with `outcome`: `partial` lists the values not live. Never report either as done (skill publishing). `warnings`: COMPONENT_SWAP_DROPS_OVERRIDES (skill components), ENTRY_STILL_DRAFT and COMPONENT_DRAFT (skill publishing). It does NOT change the field SCHEMA — use add_field (pageId) / set_page_content for that. Renaming the slug keeps content intact. Publishing copies the draft blocks live in the same call, and a singleton's content entry with them. STRUCTURED DATA is native SEO, never a field: Automatic JSON-LD from the content, unless `schemaType` picks a schema.org type or pasted `schema` (wins over both, null clears it) is set (skill seo). noindex, canonical, og and twitter set the page's head extras; each MERGES into what is stored (a key you leave out is kept, null or an empty string clears it). STRUCTURE (separate from schema): a page is composed of SECTIONS. NEVER build a page out of loose top-level heading/text/image/button/spacer blocks — they cannot be moved, duplicated or swapped as a unit, the visual editor cannot outline or name them, and every one of them becomes its own section in the editor. A hero of a headline, a lede and two CTAs is ONE section, not four. TWO SHAPES, and the choice is about REUSE. (1) A band that appears on more than one page, or that needs layout variants, is a COMPONENT with a `sectionType` — see create_component. Components sharing a `sectionType` are that section's VARIANTS (one Hero: 'Centered' for the home page and 'Two-column' for about, same prop keys so a swap keeps the content). This is also the only shape the editor's 'Add a section' picker can insert, and the only one that gets a family name and a variant switcher. (2) A genuinely one-off band on a single page is a `section` BLOCK whose `props.children` hold its blocks. THE TRADEOFF, stated in the present tense because it is real today: inside a component, ONLY the leaves a declared prop TARGETS are click-to-edit on the canvas — each declared prop's `target` is re-keyed to that PLACEMENT's own override address, so editing it changes this page and not the shared definition. A prop with no `target` still SHOWS as a dock control, but its override reaches no rendered slot, so editing it changes nothing on the page. Copy that no prop points at is worse still: no binding and no control, unreachable from click-to-edit AND from the dock, changeable only by editing the component definition, which rewrites every page that places it. A `section` block's children stay click-to-edit unconditionally. So when you choose a component, DECLARE A PROP — WITH A `target` — for every string, link and image a marketer will ever touch; a component with un-propped editable copy is the defect, not the component. In the dock an unset prop shows EMPTY and inherits the definition's default, so set props explicitly when you want the current copy visible there. An IMPORTED site's components are its own (read the repo); its nav, footer and modals are the Layout. On a blank site, do not hand-write a band's JSON: start from a built-in section blueprint (list_components returns locked `builtin:*` blueprints with no projectId — hero-centered, hero-split, feature-grid-three, cta-banner and more), each already rooted in a `section` block with its editable leaves declared as props. INLINE its blockJson as a `section` block for a one-off band; for a recurring band, materialize it with create_component `from` so it becomes project-scoped before implementation validation, Output or publication. Direct `builtin:*` component references exist only for legacy delivery compatibility. Two consecutive call-to-action buttons are two sibling `button` blocks inside the same section — never a `columns` block, which is a `repeat(N,1fr)` grid and would stretch each CTA to half the container. Buttons are inline-level and flow side by side on their own.

tools.name: push_to_github
tools.description: Commit files to the connected repository — a real git commit written server-side by the GitHub App: no clone, remote or token of your own. Send `files` ([{path, content, encoding}]) and/or `deletePaths`, plus a `message`; both go into ONE commit, so a rename is atomic. It targets the BUILD branch by default, where the push starts the rebuild that goes live — poll get_deploy_status after it, and read the response's `note`, which says whether this push deploys. Pass `branch` to push somewhere else (a branch that does not exist yet is created from the build branch, or from `baseBranch`) and then open a pull request with create_github_pull_request. Pass `expectedHeadSha` from list_github_commits — a full sha or a prefix of one — to be refused with a 409 rather than silently overwrite a branch someone else moved while you worked. Limits, enforced BEFORE anything is written: 200 paths and 10 MB per commit, and `.git`, `.github/workflows`, `.env` and `.npmrc` are never writable — a refused patch writes nothing at all and names every offending path.

tools.name: get_binding_report
tools.description: The receipt for 'is this site actually EDITABLE?'. Each release scans the built HTML for the element rendering each CMS field value; per slot this returns `mode` ('text-match' = guessed from rendered text, 'declared' = template-declared), what was bound, and `unmatched`: each path with its reason (reasons: skill bindings). DEPLOY FIRST: before any release there is no report (pages 0, mode null, refreshRequired true). `refreshReason`: a HEADLESS site never gets one (`never-generated`); `layoutRoutes` and `coverage.error`: skill bindings. `unaddressable` is the visible live text no field owns, by route (null = unmeasured: diff visible text against entry values); over `count / visible > 0.02`, fix it in the SOURCE and re-read (playbook §11). `entryRowUnbound`: a bound card's words no field of its entry claims, by route, with `reason` (reference, boolean, locale-format, counter, no-field); never also in `unaddressable`. `canvas.lane`: `none` → get_next_steps. `sectionsHeld` likewise; `unstampedIds`: no stamp.

slot.description: which release tree to read — everything here, `unaddressable` included, is measured PER SLOT, so on a promote-gated project pass 'current' to read the tree the editor frames. Defaults to the slot this project's releases land in. The response's `sha` is the build the report describes; `refreshRequired` is true when that is not the build this slot serves. Other per-slot fields: skill bindings.

branchId.description: content branch id (from list_branches); omit to work on main

tools.name: get_conversion_brief
tools.description: The per-project brief for making this site's bindings DURABLE — read it before you touch the templates. Returns what already exists in the CMS: every live page with its route, every bindable field path with its `label`, `kind`, the CMS value (`current`) and the copy the repo renders today (`original`), the exact attributes to declare, and the ordered steps. Call it for any site whose pages were DERIVED at import, and whenever get_next_steps reports `bindings-not-declared`. It REPLACES re-registering a schema: these pages, fields and values exist already, so create_page / add_field / create_content_model would build a second schema over the first — edit values with set_page_content instead. `lane`: 'git-connected' = pull_project_source returns a repo; 'archive' = a tarball. Recipe: playbook §13; get_binding_report is the finish line. Pass `complete: true` before running the CODEMOD (`npx @bettercms-ai/convert`): the brief UNCAPPED and paged, its full path list pinned under a `briefDigest` — what the coverage meter measures the build against. The complete brief also carries `forms`: wiring them and publishing the forms it names, skill bindings.

complete.description: true = the COMPLETE brief for a codemod: nothing truncated, no page omitted, paged 50 pages at a time. Page 1 pins the path list the coverage meter measures against.

cursor.description: The `cursor` from the previous page. Implies complete. A 409 BRIEF_CHANGED means the brief was re-derived mid-pagination — start again with no cursor.

tools.name: get_conversion_plan
tools.description: The APPROVED conversion a human reviewed in the BetterCMS dashboard: the exact new contents of each template file, already checked against this project's real field paths. Apply it instead of writing the bindings by hand. Check out `baseHeadOid` (the exact commit it was written against), branch from there, write each file's `content` verbatim (whole file, no merge, no reformatting), then push or deploy however this project ships. `stale.head` / `stale.brief` say the repository or the CMS moved since it was approved: stop and ask for a fresh proposal. `receipt.paths.pending` lists every field the codemod could NOT bind, each with a reason (`DIALECT_UNSUPPORTED`, `PROP_TARGET_NOT_FOUND`, `REPEATER_FIXED_LENGTH`, …) — apply the plan first, then bind those by hand. Then finish as a hand conversion does: get_binding_report until `unmatched` is empty, then set_binding_mode { declaredBindings: true } and release once more. 404 with `code: "no-approved-plan"` means nobody has approved one: use get_conversion_brief and do the conversion yourself. Requires artifact:write; on a workspace-wide connection pass `projectId`.

tools.name: get_site_composition

Call it before a whole-site componentize run (playbook §12) and after it, as the proof. Per page: `kind`, a block census, `nonComponentBlocks` and every `component` placement with its `status` (a draft renders as an EMPTY STRING on the live site), `inPicker` and `emptyRequiredProps`. Site-wide: counts, `awaitingApproval` (a HUMAN approves in the dashboard; no tool here can), `notInPicker`, `unused` and `layout.placements`. Each field: skill components. `verdict.everyPageComposed` with `verdict.reasons` is the answer to give the user. Pages are read DRAFT-inclusive: check each page's own `status` before claiming the site is live.

tools.name: get_componentize_plan
tools.description: What this site's SECTIONS would become as components — a proposal that creates nothing and is computed live. For a site whose pages were DERIVED at import, each top-level field GROUP is one section: `hero-*` and `faq-*` keys, and the repeaters the import folded (`group-*`). Per page: each section's `groupKey`, `sectionType` family, leaf `fields` with their CMS values, `shapeHash`, and either the component already rendering it (`reuse.componentId`) or the proposed one (`reuse.proposedSlug`). Under `components`, a NEW one carries the exact `props` and `blockJson` create_component would take; an EXISTING one only `componentId`, `slug` and `name` (nothing is written for it). `pending` says why a group is not offered (its codes: see `summary`). Per-page components, collection templates and chrome (never a section): skill componentize. READ `summary: true` FIRST — the full plan runs to hundreds of KB; `paged` pages it (409 PLAN_CHANGED = start again); the unpaged full read is what `--plan plan.json` takes. Keep the `digest` — componentize_sections refuses any other.

summary.description: true = no values: each section's groupKey, family, pending and component slug. Read this first. `pending` codes (each explained in skill componentize): `NO_GROUP_ROOT`, `NOT_A_SECTION` (`detail`: `ENTRY_METADATA`, `DECLINED`), `IMAGE_AS_TEXT`, `ALREADY_COMPONENTIZED`, `EMPTY_GROUP`, `NESTED_REPEATER`, `PAGE_NOT_EMPTY`, `COMPONENTIZE_DROPS_LEAF` (the section binds a value the instance would neither own nor keep, so it is not converted: it stays editable on the page; log its groupKey), `HOLLOW_INSTANCE` (every value stays on the page: no instance). A section's `instance.kept` lists page paths that stay the page's; `TYPE_NOT_PROPPABLE` there is a bound value no prop type expresses, kept bound on the page as before: nothing to do.

paged.description: true = 10 pages at a time; the response carries `page`, `pageCount` and a `cursor` for the next.

cursor.description: The `cursor` from the previous page. Implies paged. A 409 `PLAN_CHANGED` means start again with no cursor.

tools.name: componentize_sections
tools.description: Turn this site's derived sections into components. CONFIRM WITH THE USER FIRST: show them get_componentize_plan's sections, how many components it will create and which pages it will rewrite; `dryRun` first. It creates each proposed component as a DRAFT and replaces each page's DRAFT blocks with ordered `component` instances, one per group. The page keeps its `fields`, values and bindings (see `copy`). Pass the plan's `digest`; a 409 `stale-plan` means the site changed: read the plan again, show the user what changed and confirm again. Read `components.wouldDuplicate` first (skill components). Re-running is safe: a placed group returns as ALREADY_COMPONENTIZED. DRAFTS ONLY — an unpublished component renders as an EMPTY STRING on the live site, so publish_component each one and publish the pages, then call it again with `codemod: true` for the repository half (skill componentize). A group the user says is NOT a section: `decline: true` with those `sections` (skill componentize).

digest.description: The `digest` get_componentize_plan returned. A different one is refused with 409 stale-plan.

pageIds.description: Componentize only these pages (ids from the plan). Omit for every page the plan lists.

pages.description: The same page filter under the name the dashboard uses. Unioned with pageIds; an EMPTY list is refused rather than treated as every page.

sections.description: Act only on these section groupKeys (from the plan); every other section keeps its placement.

copy.description: Who owns each section's copy. 'bind' (default) leaves it in the page fields. 'instance' moves it onto each placement; the page's fields are KEPT and marked `origin: "componentized"` (skill componentize).

dryRun.description: true = return the receipt without writing anything. Do this first.

group.description: File the components this run creates into this Component Group (by NAME, created when missing), else its section family (skill componentize). A reused component keeps its Group; the receipt's `components.groups` lists the Groups filed into.

decline.description: true = record `sections` as NOT sections (nothing is componentized; the plan stops proposing them). false = offer them again. Needs `sections`.

joinTwins.description: true = move each locale copy (`/fr`) still on its own component onto its twin's (`bindPaths` keeps its fields). A dry run lists each in `joins`. Whole plan only.

codemod.description: true = componentize nothing; run the section-order codemod in the connected repo on its own Actions, which commits for the next build. After the components and pages are published. `skipped` = no repo to commit to: its `run` is the `convert --sections` command and --pages file for your checkout, then submit_sections_receipt

instructions: Start every project with get_next_steps: its `receipt` lists what is done (`done`), what is missing (`missing`, each citing its count) and the one `nextAction`. Work from it instead of re-reading the site, and call it again after each batch of edits and before you report. On an imported site the gate is the definition of done: run `receipt.gate.nextAction`, read again, and repeat until `receipt.complete` is true. Record a gap you cannot close with editor_setup `exempt` only for an allowed reason that is true, with a note, never in prose. Never stop a setup to ask the user: authoring (components) and media (the CDN) are recorded for you, and your prompt says whether you may push. Report what was decided. TOOL SCHEMAS: a client with tool search lists most BetterCMS tools by name only. Before the first call to a tool whose schema you have not been shown, load it with the client's tool search, and load every tool the task needs in ONE search (for a renaming pass: update_field, update_content_model, update_component, list_components). A call made without the schema is refused by the client before it reaches BetterCMS ("Invalid tool parameters"): that is this, never a BetterCMS error, and never a reason to change the arguments. When the user asks to make a site or all of its pages editable and they were DERIVED at import: editor_setup, then get_next_steps until `receipt.gate.complete`. To convert its source or bind its fields: this is playbook §13. Read `bettercms://playbook/schema` §13, call get_binding_report and get_conversion_brief { complete: true }, convert EVERY route the brief lists, and finish only when get_binding_report shows coverage.pending empty on every route — not when the first page works. On a workspace-wide connection pass projectId on every call; never ask the user to re-scope the connection. When the user asks to make the navigation, footer or other site chrome editable, or get_next_steps lists a `layout-*` or `chrome-duplicated` item: this is playbook §11 item 3. Chrome is the project Layout, never page fields: in the source, wrap each Section in `data-bcms-layout-section` (the slot, its base slug) and mark each value `data-bcms-layout-field="layout:<sections[slug].id>:<fieldId>"`, never `data-bcms-field` inside it, then push; the strip removes the page copies, never delete them by hand. On a site BetterCMS serves, publish_layout writes Layout VALUES into the live pages; a structure change waits for a Rebuild. Never place nav, footer or modal blocks or fields on a page: the Layout (or the site's own layout) draws chrome, so a page copy either duplicates it or renders nowhere (get_componentize_plan reports one as LAYOUT_CHROME). A call to action is ONE `button` field (value {label, href, variant?, size?, arrow?, icon?, newTab?}), rendered with BcmsButton from @bettercms-ai/astro or @bettercms-ai/next: never a text field beside a link field. A page that already holds such a pair (primaryCtaText + primaryCtaHref) becomes one button with update_field `mergeHref`. Inside a component a CTA is a `button` block whose text and href two props target. Names are 1-2 words of meaning per part: playbook §2 Naming. When the user asks to componentize the whole site, to turn every section into a component, or to build a component library from the site: this is playbook §12. Read `bettercms://playbook/schema` §12, start with get_site_composition, and use the batch tools — componentize_sections, compose_pages, update_layout with `commands`, publish_components — rather than one call per component. Finish with get_site_composition and tell the user what the platform does not model (cookie banners, modals, breadcrumbs, pagination) and which components still need the owner's approval in the dashboard before they can be published. After you create collections or pages, organise them per the structure playbook: read bettercms://playbook/structure, call suggest_content_structure (read-only), show the user its outline, then apply it with set_content_structure and the version it returned (the If-Match). A project that already has a structure keeps it: file only what you created, with move_to_folder, unless the user asks for a full re-organisation. Before writing code in a repo that uses BetterCMS, explore the repo, then read the installed `bettercms` skill (`npx @bettercms-ai/install --project -y` adds it if missing): its table turns what you found into the one reference the task needs — read only that. Without the skill installed, read the same files as resources: bettercms://skill/bettercms, then bettercms://skill/<reference>. How fields and props look in the editor (groups, tabs, rows, icons, item names) is playbook §14 or the `field-ui` prompt: write it with update_content_model field* or update_component prop* plus ifMatch, read it back, and finish when get_next_steps reports no dock-* step. An item an author held back from site publishes (`publishHeldAt` set) stays out of whole-site publishes: do not publish it unless the user names it; publish_entries `release` includes it again.
